canonical_statement: The study emulated a target trial to compare the cardiovascular effectiveness of initiating empagliflozin versus dapagliflozin, in addition to standard care, among adults with treated type 2 diabetes.

Eligible individuals had treated type 2 diabetes and were receiving antihyperglycemic treatment other than insulin monotherapy during the enrollment period from June 1, 2014, through October 31, 2020.

canonical_statement: The study used nationwide Danish health registries linked at the individual level through the Civil Personal Registration number, allowing long-term follow-up for death and emigration.
The authors specified a hypothetical pragmatic target trial and emulated it with observational data from Denmark.
The emulated randomization used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weights.

Treatment weights controlled for 57 potential confounders spanning demographics, diabetes duration and laboratory values, comorbidities, glucose-lowering and other medications, socioeconomic variables, health-care seeking, and calendar year.
Multiple imputation by fully conditional specification with 10 imputations addressed missing hemoglobin A1c, kidney function, lipid, civil status, employment, income, and education data.

The primary intention-to-treat analysis estimated weighted incidence and cumulative incidence with the Aalen-Johansen estimator and treated death as a competing event for nonfatal outcomes and noncardiovascular death as a competing event for cardiovascular death.
The study estimated 6-year absolute risks, risk differences, and risk ratios comparing empagliflozin with dapagliflozin.
The per-protocol analysis censored treatment changes and used inverse probability of censoring weights with baseline and time-updated covariates.
Nonparametric bootstrapping with 500 samples generated percentile-based 95% confidence intervals, and Rubin's Rule pooled estimates across imputations.

Prespecified subgroup analyses covered ASCVD, heart failure, age, sex, diabetes duration, hemoglobin A1c, eGFR, number of other diabetes medications, calendar year, civil status, employment, income, and education.
Sensitivity analyses truncated treatment weights at 10 and broadened cardiovascular death identification to include both underlying and immediate causes of death.
The maximum overall inverse probability of treatment weight was 12.0; subgroup maxima were larger, including 23.9 with ASCVD and 21.7 for eGFR below 45 mL/min/1.73 m².
The eligible cohort included 36,670 empagliflozin initiators and 20,606 dapagliflozin initiators.
Before weighting, median age was about 62 years, 37% to 38% were female, median diabetes duration was about 8 years, median hemoglobin A1c was 8.2%, and median eGFR was 87 to 88 mL/min/1.73 m².

Before weighting, empagliflozin initiators had more ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, stable angina, and insulin use and less DPP-4 inhibitor use than dapagliflozin initiators; measured covariates were well balanced after weighting.
Median follow-up was 3.2 years with an interquartile range of 2.1 to 4.7 years.

During follow-up, treatment discontinuation occurred in 40% of empagliflozin initiators and 45% of dapagliflozin initiators, while switching to another SGLT2 inhibitor occurred in 1.2% and 4.5%, respectively.
Within 6 years, 2,265 MACEs occurred among empagliflozin initiators and 1,278 among dapagliflozin initiators.
In the intention-to-treat analysis, the adjusted 6-year MACE risk was 10.0% with empagliflozin and 10.0% with dapagliflozin; the risk ratio was 1.00 (95% CI 0.91 to 1.11).

canonical_statement: The authors reported no noteworthy MACE differences across subgroups defined by sex, diabetes duration, hemoglobin A1c, eGFR, number of antihyperglycemic medications, calendar year, income, or education.
Treatment assignment was not random, so unmeasured confounding could remain despite the target-trial emulation and measured-covariate weighting.
Publication of EMPA-REG OUTCOME in 2015 could have shifted patients with higher cardiovascular risk toward empagliflozin and introduced calendar-time prescribing bias.
Cardiovascular death could be misclassified because the autopsy rate in Denmark was below 10%.
The apparent modifying effects of age, civil status, and employment could be chance findings because the study performed many analyses; the authors considered them exploratory pending confirmation.
The cardiovascular effectiveness associated with initiating empagliflozin or dapagliflozin was not different in people with treated type 2 diabetes.

The authors stated that the findings support an SGLT2 inhibitor class-effect assumption for empagliflozin and dapagliflozin but do not establish a class effect for all SGLT2 inhibitors without comparisons of the remaining agents.

The authors stated that, given no observed cardiovascular outcome difference, drug-cost differences would likely translate into cost-effectiveness differences if other relevant outcomes were equivalent.
